results.title: Recursively enumerable subgroup of a free group

results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F$ be the free group on the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. results.title: Solvable word problem for a quotient of a free group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ be the free group on the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and let $N$ be a subgroup of $F$. The word problem for $F / N$ is solvable when membership in $N$ is decidable: the predicate on words $w$ (finite lists of letters, each a generator together with a sign) that the image of $w$ in $F$ lies in $N$ is computable.

results.title: Solvable conjugacy problem for a quotient of a free group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ be the free group on the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and let $N$ be a subgroup of $F$. The conjugacy problem for $F / N$ is solvable when the predicate on pairs of words $(w, v)$ (finite lists of letters, each a generator together with a sign) that some $u \in F$ satisfies $u w u^{-1} v^{-1} \in N$, with $w$ and $v$ read as elements of $F$, is computable.

results.title: Completeness of the Boolean certificate verifier
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a circuit over the Boolean signature with $n$ inputs, $s$ gates and one output, and let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be truth values on which the output of $c$ under the Boolean interpretation is true. Let $b$ be the array $(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}, v_0, \dots, v_{s-1})$, where $v_j$ is the value of gate $j$ of $c$ on input $x$. Then $b$ has length $n + s$ and the Boolean certificate verifier accepts $b$.

results.title: Short accepted certificates exist exactly for satisfiable circuits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a circuit over the Boolean signature with $n$ inputs, $s$ gates and one output. The Boolean certificate verifier accepts some array of at most $n + 2s$ truth values if and only if there are truth values $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ on which the output of $c$ under the Boolean interpretation is true.

results.title: Cost of the Boolean certificate verifier
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a circuit over the Boolean signature with $n$ inputs, $s$ gates and one output, and let $b$ be an array of $m$ truth values. The cost counted by the Boolean certificate verifier on $b$ is $2 + s + \sum_{j < s} a_j$ if $m = n + s$, where $a_j$ is the number of arguments of gate $j$, and $1$ otherwise.

results.title: Linear cost of the Boolean certificate verifier
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a natural number and let $c$ be a circuit over the Boolean signature with $n$ inputs, $s$ gates and one output in which every gate has at most $K$ arguments. Then for every array $b$ of truth values, the cost counted by the Boolean certificate verifier on $b$ is at most $2 + (K + 1)s$.

results.title: Circuit-satisfiability instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of circuit satisfiability is a pair $(n, G)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of variables, and a finite list $G$ of gates, each gate a triple $(o, a, b)$ of natural numbers: an operation code $o$, a first input $a$ and a second input $b$.

results.title: Resolving a circuit input
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an assignment $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ of booleans to the variables and the list $v = (v_0, \dots, v_{k-1})$ of the values of the gates evaluated so far, an input index $r$ resolves to $x_r$ if $r < n$, to $v_{r-n}$ if $n \le r < n + k$, and to false if $r \ge n + k$.

results.title: Value of a gate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be an assignment of booleans to the variables and $v$ the list of values of the earlier gates. An input index $r$ resolves to $x_r$ if $r < n$, and otherwise to $v_{r-n}$, or to false if that entry does not exist. The value of a gate $(o, a, b)$ is the conjunction of the resolved inputs $a$ and $b$ if $o = 0$, their disjunction if $o = 1$, the negation of the resolved input $a$ if…

results.title: Evaluating a circuit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an assignment of booleans to the variables and a list of gates $g_1, \dots, g_m$, circuit evaluation returns the list $(v_1, \dots, v_m)$ of gate values, where $v_k$ is the value of the gate $g_k$ under the assignment and the earlier values $(v_1, \dots, v_{k-1})$.

results.title: Well-formed circuit-satisfiability instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, G)$ with gates $G = (g_0, \dots, g_{m-1})$ is well formed when every gate $g_j = (o, a, b)$ satisfies $o \le 5$, and moreover: if $o = 0$ or $o = 1$ then $a < n + j$ and $b < n + j$; if $o = 2$ then $a < n + j$; and if $o = 3$ then $a < n$.

results.title: Satisfiable circuit instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, G)$ is satisfiable when there is an assignment $x \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n$ of booleans to the $n$ variables such that the evaluation of the circuit $G$ under $x$ has a last gate value and that value is true. In particular an instance with no gates is not satisfiable.

results.title: The CIRCUIT SAT decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: CIRCUIT SAT is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $s$ exactly when $s$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of circuit-satisfiability instances, to an instance that is well formed and satisfiable. Bitstrings that fail to decode are rejected.

results.title: CIRCUIT SAT is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The CIRCUIT SAT decision problem on bitstrings belongs to the class NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.

results.title: Blum complexity measure
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A Blum measure $\Phi$ assigns to every program $c$ and input $n \in \mathbb{N}$ a partially defined cost $\Phi_c(n) \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfying Blum's two axioms: $\Phi_c(n)$ is defined exactly when program $c$ halts on input $n$, and the relation $\Phi_c(n) = m$ between $c$, $n$ and $m$ is decidable.

results.title: Blum complexity class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a Blum measure $\Phi$ and a function $t$ from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$, the Blum class of $t$ consists of the partial functions $f$ from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$ that are computed by some program $c$ whose cost $\Phi_c(n)$ is defined and at most $t(n)$ for all but finitely many inputs $n$.

results.title: Blum classes are monotone in the bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `t` is eventually dominated by `t'`, every function in the `t`-class is in the `t'`-class.

results.title: Blum classes via an explicit threshold
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Phi$ be a Blum measure, $t$ a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$ and $f$ a partial function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$. Then $f$ lies in the Blum class of $t$ with respect to $\Phi$ if and only if there are a program $c$ that computes $f$ and a threshold $N$ such that for every input $n \ge N$ the cost $\Phi_c(n)$ is defined and at most $t(n)$.

results.title: The PCP theorem: NP = PCP(O(log n), O(1))
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A decision problem belongs to NP if and only if, for some natural numbers $c$ and $q$, it belongs to $\mathrm{PCP}(r, s)$, where the randomness bound is $r(n) = c \lfloor \log_2(n + 1) \rfloor$ and the query bound is the constant function $s(n) = q$.

results.summary: A negative sender installs the dual continuation on the positive role; reordering the distinct insertions retains the same complete bound pair.

results.title: Outer lookups pass through a freshly bound pair
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An outer lifted role lookup passes through both fresh bound entries and reflects to the exact old external capability.

results.title: Dual advancement under restriction splits into inner and outer cases
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Exact pure restriction projection. An internal matched pair changes only the bound pair at the same rank; an outer matched pair changes only the external context and retains the entire old bound pair.

results.title: Outer dual advancement lifts through restriction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An actual external matched update lifts through restriction without altering its private pair, even when the payload protocol refers to private data.

results.title: Dual advancement under restriction splits, keeping the private step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Projection additionally retains an actual private old-head/continuation transition when the communication is hidden by ν. It does not reduce private advancement to an arbitrary capability with the same rank.

results.title: Inversion of endpoint typing for restriction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Restriction inversion exposes the actual bound dual pair.

results.title: Endpoint typing is preserved by forward scope extrusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The forward canonical scope rule preserves the exact external context and ambient depth, with the dual pair derived from restriction typing.

results.title: Endpoint typing absorbs a role absent from its parallel partner
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A role missing from one component can be reattached only after actual absence in its typed partner derives completion of the advertised capability.

results.title: Endpoint typing restores both bound roles to the restricted side
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the actual scope split, either freshly bound role can be moved back to the restricted component only when partner absence proves it completed.

results.title: Endpoint typing is preserved by reverse scope extrusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Reverse scope transport recovers the exact external ownership split from the actual restriction/parallel typing, with no closed-hole premise.

results.title: Endpoint typing is invariant under scope extrusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Both directions of the canonical scope congruence preserve exact external polarized ownership and the unchanged ambient binder depth.

results.title: Parallel commutation preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Parallel commutation swaps a derived disjoint split, not its capabilities.

results.title: Parallel reassociation preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Parallel reassociation preserves the actual three-way disjoint split.

results.title: Reverse parallel reassociation preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Reverse reassociation recovers both sub-splits from the supplied typing.

results.title: Adding a parallel nil preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Adding a parallel nil allocates it no ownership; no active slot is dropped.

results.title: Removing a restriction around nil preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Restriction of nil has exactly the completed external ownership of nil.

results.title: Adding a restriction around nil preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A completed fresh pair may be introduced around nil while retaining all original external capabilities and scope.

results.title: Swapping nested restrictions preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Nested restriction commutation swaps their derived complete dual pairs.

results.title: Reverse restriction swap preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Reverse nested restriction commutation uses the canonical involution.

results.title: Structural congruence preserves endpoint typing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every existing canonical structural congruence preserves endpoint typing in both directions with exactly the same depth and ownership. Unsupported choice/replication shapes are rejected by the typing-derived finite invariant.

results.title: Compatibility restricts to the left part of a union
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Left children inherit actual peer compatibility.

results.title: Compatibility restricts to the right part of a disjoint union
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A disjoint right child inherits actual peer compatibility without shadowing.

results.title: Binding a dual private pair preserves compatibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A chosen exact dual private pair extends a semantically compatible interface.

results.title: Binding a dual private pair preserves balance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At a semantically balanced outer interface, binding an exact dual private pair retains balance for the pair and every actual outer peer.

results.title: Semantic advance under a private binding is private or outer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Faithful projection retains an actual private-pair advance OR the actual outer advance and unchanged bound pair. It never chooses an arbitrary Xi.

results.title: Outer semantic advances lift past a private binding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An actual outer semantic advance lifts without changing its private pair.

results.title: Equivalent retyping preserves semantic balance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pointwise semantic recoding retains actual paired domain and cap ranks.

results.title: Union of disjoint balanced contexts is balanced
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Disjoint balanced components form a balanced ownership frame union.

results.title: Injective rekeying preserves dual compatibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Injective physical-name rekeying retains partial dual compatibility.

results.title: Binding a fresh dual pair preserves dual compatibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A fresh complete bound pair extends any ordinary compatible interface.

results.title: Subject reduction for endpoint typing at compatible interfaces
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: From a typed source at an initially compatible interface, all five canonical reduction constructors preserve typing and compatibility, with one matched external subject-pair advancement or an unchanged interface when communication is private. No fragment or enabled-edge premise is required.

results.title: Subject reduction for endpoint typing at balanced interfaces
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A typed source with a balanced initial interface retains typing and balance after any canonical step. Balance supplies the required compatibility; the exact zero-or-one external advancement evidence is retained.

results.title: Subject reduction for endpoint typing at the empty interface
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An empty-interface typed network retains empty-interface typing through any canonical step. The empty context is balanced, hence compatible, including communication behind restrictions and pre/post congruence.
